sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Context**: The conferences were necessitated by the **Simon Commission's** rejection by Indian nationalists and the need for a 'consensus' on the future **Dominion Status**.
• **Mechanism**: The British aimed to bypass the **Indian National Congress (INC)** by inviting Princely States and minority representatives to create a 'divide and rule' framework.
• **Outcome**: The conferences laid the structural blueprint for the **Government of India Act, 1935**.
• **Key Metric**: The INC participated only in the Second Round Table Conference (RTC) following the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**.

items.definition: The central point of contention regarding separate electorates for minorities, specifically the Depressed Classes, which led to the Communal Award.
The proposed constitutional framework involving the integration of British India and Princely States into a single federation.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Federalism**: Introduction of the concept of an All-India Federation.
• **Minority Rights**: Formalization of the demand for separate electorates by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Lack of consensus between INC and minority groups; British insistence on 'safeguards'.
• **Solutions**: The Poona Pact (1932) emerged as a compromise to the Communal Award, bypassing the RTC deadlock.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: '1-2-3: Boy-Man-Boy'.
• **Decoded Meaning**: 1st RTC: Boycotted by INC; 2nd RTC: Man (Gandhi) attended; 3rd RTC: Boycotted by INC.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often asks if the INC attended all three. Remember: INC attended ONLY the Second RTC.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Constitutional Deadlock' to describe the failure of the RTCs to reconcile nationalist aspirations with imperial interests.

keyTakeaways: The RTCs marked the shift from 'Dominion Status' to 'Provincial Autonomy' as the primary British offer.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar attended all three conferences, representing the Depressed Classes.
The failure of the RTCs directly led to the resumption of the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1932.
